title: Technology Sector Update for 06/08/2018: BABA,QCOM,NXPI,BABA,AAPL
text:
Shutterstock photo Top Tech Stocks
MSFT +0.75%
AAPL -1.02%
IBM +0.52%
CSCO -0.44%
GOOG -0.35%
Technology stocks fell Friday, including steep declines for chipmakers, with shares of tech companies in the S&P 500 dropping about 0.2% in value today. The Philadelphia semiconductor index recorded a nearly 0.9% retreat.
In sector news,
+ Alibaba ( BABA ) closed little changed Friday afternoon in a range-bound session, swinging about 1% either side of Thursday's closing price, after the Chinese internet conglomerate saying its Ant Financial affiliate has raised $14 billion in Series C equity financing. The latest funding round included a RMB-denominated tranche for the company from domestic investors and a dollar-denominated tranche from international sources. Ant Financial expects to use the new proceeds to accelerate globalization plans for its Alipay blockchain platform in addition to supporting its artificial intelligence, cyber-security and internet-of-things capabilities.
- Qualcomm Inc ( QCOM ) was extending its declines Friday, falling over 1% in recent trading after the specialty chipmaker again pushed out the deadline for NXP Semiconductors NV ( NXPI ) shareholders to tender their shares under Qualcomm's $127-per-share buyout offer by another week to June 15. Through the close of business on Thursday, investors have tendered just over 17.7 million NXP Semi shares, or roughly 5.1% of the company's outstanding stock, down from a peak of 65.3 million shares tendered in early March.
- Apple ( AAPL ) stumbled Friday, dropping nearly 2%, following reports the tech giant has been scaling back on component orders for iPhones due out later this year. Apple last year ordered enough components to produce up to 100 million units of its iPhone 8, iPhone 8 Plus and iPhone X models but this year is expecting to ship only 80 million units, two people told the Nikkei Asian Review. Suppliers also are being told to be ready sooner for two new iPhone models using organic light-emitting diode displays in hopes of avoiding the delays Apple experienced last year, the industry sources reportedly said.
